title: Messi's Magic 8th Goal Puts Him on Top in World Cup Golden Boot Race!
summary: Wow! The race for the World Cup's Golden Boot just got even more exciting. Lionel Messi, the superstar from Argentina, scored his eighth goal in a nail-biting 3-2 win over Egypt on Tuesday. That goal put him back in the lead for the award given to the tournament's top scorer. Just days ago, he was tied with France's Kylian Mbappe at seven goals each. But then Norway's Erling Haaland scored twice against Brazil, making it a three-way tie at seven! Now Messi has pulled ahead again. But it's still super close. Mbappe can catch up when France plays Morocco on Thursday. England's Harry Kane has six goals, and Spain's Mikel Oyarzabal has four. If two players end up with the same number of goals, the winner is the one with more assists (passes that lead to a goal). If that's still tied, they look at who played fewer minutes. No one has ever won the Golden Boot twice, but Mbappe, Kane, and Colombia's James Rodriguez are all trying to be the first. The record for most goals in a single World Cup is 13, set by France's Just Fontaine way back in 1958. That's like scoring almost two goals per game! Can Messi or Mbappe break that record? We'll have to watch and see.
why_it_matters: Just like in your own sports or games, getting to the top and staying ahead can be a tight race where every point matters.

background_read: The World Cup Golden Boot award has been given to the tournament's top goal scorer since the very first World Cup in 1930.
Famous winners in the past include Brazil's Ronaldo and Argentina's Gabriel Batistuta.
Just Fontaine (a French striker) set the incredible record of 13 goals in 1958, and no one has beaten it yet.
